title: Variant memory spectra calibration for long-context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Lina Zhao
description: Problem: Long-context variants of Llama, Mistral and Qwen present very different KV working-set shapes across sequence lengths and batch mixes. The current single-profile allocator causes either excessive fragmentation or OOMs when sequences > 2048 tokens are common. Goal: Create per-variant 'memory spectra' (a small parametric curve) that maps observed sequence-length percentiles and batch size distribution to allocation/residency targets and eviction bias. Use these spectra to drive allocator slab assignment, KV residency thresholds, and continuous-batching heuristics so that long-context workloads remain within SLOs without overprovisioning GPU memory. Scope: offline profiling, lightweight online estimator, allocator changes (spectra hints), KV eviction policy tuning, benchmark harness and canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Automated profiler generates a spectra artifact for each tested model-variant (Llama-2-13B-long, Mistral-27B-long, Qwen-14B-8192) and stores it in /artifacts/memory-spectra/
Runtime reads spectra and applies slab allocation hints to reduce fragmentation measured by free-slab variance by >= 40% compared to baseline for long sequences
KV eviction rate (evictions/min) reduced by >= 60% at equivalent throughput for workloads with median sequence length >= 2048
End-to-end 95th percentile latency for sample long-context chat workload remains <= 350ms under target throughput and batcher settings
No increase in token-level cost > 5% after enabling spectra-based allocation for dedicated instances
Canary rollout plan exists and a rollback path to the previous allocator is validated in QA cluster
implementation_steps: Phase 1: Profiling harness — extend existing sampler to capture sequence-length histogram, per-request kv-residency footprint, and per-token memory churn across model-variants (deliverable: spectra proto)
Phase 2: Offline analysis — fit 3-parameter spectra curve (working_set_scale, residency_slope, eviction_bias) per variant and validate against held-out traces
Phase 3: Allocator integration — expose spectra hints to slab allocator and KV manager; implement 'spectra-aware slab packing' and 'weighted-evict' policy
Phase 4: Batcher coordination — update continuous-batching policy to consult spectra for target batch size distribution and early flush thresholds for long sequences
Phase 5: Benchmarks and canary — run end-to-end perf tests (2048/4096/8192 seq mixes), deploy canary, gather dashboards and iteratively tune parameters
Phase 6: Rollout & monitoring — gradual ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% with synthetic and customer traffic, add observability (spectra mismatch alerts)
notes_and_risks: Risk: Spectra overfitting to sampled traces — mitigated by cross-validation and periodic re-profiling (weekly automated job)
Risk: Interaction with quant-aware memory layouts may change slab sizes — we will include quant-mode in profiling matrix and gate spectra by quantization profile
Trade-off: Aggressive eviction bias reduces memory pressure but can increase model recompute; we will bound eviction_bias to maintain token cost delta <= 5%
Operational: Need a small on-disk compact representation for spectra (<= 1KB) for fast lookup in cold start paths
Backwards compatibility: If spectra unavailable, runtime should fallback to 'generic-longctx' heuristic
metrics_to_track: KV hit rate and evictions per minute
average batch size and batch size distribution
